how_to_apply: Download the application form in Annexure I from the official district website or detailed notification PDF.
Fill out the application form entirely in the handwriting of the candidate.
Paste a recent passport-size photograph at the top right of the application form and sign across it.

Enclose self-attested copies of the SSC certificate, educational and professional qualification certificates and marks memos, experience certificates with appointment orders and proof of payment, study certificates from Class I to VII (or residence certificate), community certificate (if age relaxation is claimed), Bar Council enrolment certificate (where applicable), and identity proof.

Hand over the application form with enclosures and two passport size photographs at the Inward Section of the Collectorate, Integrated District Offices Complex, Jangaon, between 09.10.2026 and 15.10.2026 (10.30 AM to 5.00 PM on working days, up to 1.00 PM on Saturday, 10.10.2026) to receive the hall ticket across the counter.
Alternatively, send applications by registered post or speed post to reach the Collectorate by 5.00 PM on 15.10.2026, ensuring the cover is superscribed with the name of the post.
important_instructions: A candidate may apply for one post only. Applications will not be received at the office of the District Welfare Officer or in the Unit. Experience will be counted only if the certificate shows the post held, joining and relieving dates, and is supported by appointment orders and proof of payment. Field work, internships, project work as a student, and voluntary service are excluded. NGO experience certificates must carry the organisation registration number and NGO Darpan identity number where available. Admission to the written examination is provisional. Candidates must report by 9.00 AM on the exam day with the hall ticket, original identity card, original certificates, and a blue or black ball point pen. No entry after 9.45 AM. Mobile phones, calculators, and other electronic devices are strictly prohibited in the examination hall. The engagement is on contract basis with the District Child Protection Society for one year at a time and confers no right to regularisation. Verification of antecedents by the Police is mandatory prior to appointment. Selected candidates must provide particulars to the Police team at the venue during the oral test. Local candidates of Jangaon District as per Telangana Public Employment Order 2018 will be selected first in order of merit. Non-local candidates will be considered only if no local candidate is found eligible.

content_sections.heading: DCPU Jangaon Vacancy Details (Post-wise)
content_sections.text: The recruitment drive aims to fill 12 contractual vacancies across various designations under the District Child Protection Unit, Jangaon.

content_sections.heading: DCPU Jangaon Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: The qualifications and experience for each post are laid down under Mission Vatsalya and will not be relaxed. A higher qualification in the same subject is accepted in place of the degree prescribed. Qualifications and experience must be held on the date of the notification (08.10.2026). District Child Protection Officer: At least 3 years of work with the Government or a non-Government organisation in documentation, training and capacity building, project formulation or implementation, monitoring and supervision, preferably in women and child development or social welfare. Proficiency in computers. Protection Officer (Institutional Care & Non-Institutional Care): For a candidate with the degree alone, 2 years of work in project formulation or implementation, monitoring and supervision, preferably in women and child development or social welfare. Proficiency in computers. Legal cum Probation Officer: At least 2 years of work with the Government or a non-Government organisation or in legal matters, preferably in the rights of women and children. Good understanding of the rights and protection of women and children. Counsellor: At least 1 year of work with the Government or a non-Government organisation, preferably in women and child development. Proficiency in computers. Social Worker: Weightage for experience. Proficiency in computers. Accountant: At least 1 year of work in accounts. Computer skills and command of Tally. Data Analyst: Weightage for experience. Proficiency in computers. Assistant cum Data Entry Operator: Weightage for experience. Outreach Worker: Good communication skills. Weightage for experience.

content_sections.heading: DCPU Jangaon Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection will be by a written examination followed, on the same day, by an oral test of 25 marks. The selection list will be declared the same day. For posts at Sl.No.1 to 9: The paper carries 200 objective questions for 90 minutes, in English. Part A of 100 questions is common to these posts. Part B of 100 questions is on the subject of the post applied for. For posts at Sl.No.10 to 12: The paper carries 100 objective questions for 60 minutes, in English and Telugu, and is common to these posts. Marking Scheme: Each question has five options and carries one mark. One fourth of a mark will be deducted for every wrong answer. Nothing is deducted for a question left unanswered. Answers are marked on an OMR answer sheet. Experience Weightage: For the posts of Social Worker, Data Analyst, Assistant cum Data Entry Operator and Outreach Worker, two marks will be added for each completed year of paid work in child protection or in the field of the post, up to ten marks. Candidates will be called for verification of original certificates and the oral test in the order of marks at three candidates for each vacancy. In the oral test, each candidate will answer five questions drawn from a question bank, marked out of five by the Selection Committee. The selection list will be drawn in the order of total marks. Where totals are equal, higher marks in the written examination and then older age will determine priority.

Alternatively, send applications by registered post or speed post to reach the Collectorate by 5.00 PM on 15.10.2026, ensuring the cover is superscribed with the name of the post.

faq.question: Q1. What is DCPU Jangaon Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: DCPU Jangaon Recruitment 2026 is an official notification issued by the Office of the Collector and District Magistrate, Jangaon, to fill 12 contract vacancies under Mission Vatsalya in the District Child Protection Unit.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are available in DCPU Jangaon Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: A total of 12 vacancies are available across various posts, including District Child Protection Officer, Protection Officers, Legal cum Probation Officer, Counsellor, Social Workers, Accountant, Data Analyst, Assistant cum Data Entry Operator, and Outreach Workers.

faq.question: Q3. What is the last date to apply for DCPU Jangaon Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: The last date to submit applications is 15 October 2026 up to 5:00 PM.

faq.question: Q4. What is the educational qualification required for DCPU Jangaon posts?
faq.answer: Qualifications vary by post, ranging from Class XII pass for Outreach Workers and DEO to professional degrees like LL.B. for Legal cum Probation Officer and Post Graduate degrees in Social Work, Sociology, Child Development, or related fields for managerial posts.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for DCPU Jangaon Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Candidates must have completed 21 years and should not have completed 35 years of age as on 01.10.2026, with upper age relaxation of five years for SC, ST, and BC candidates, and service-based relaxation for personnel already working in the Unit.

faq.question: Q6. Is there an application fee for DCPU Jangaon Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: No, the notification specifies that there is no application fee.

faq.question: Q7. How can I apply for DCPU Jangaon Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Applications must be submitted offline by filling out the prescribed form by hand and submitting it either in person at the Inward Section of the Collectorate, Jangaon, or by sending it via registered post or speed post.

faq.question: Q8. When is the written examination scheduled?
faq.answer: The written examination is scheduled for Friday, 16 October 2026 (10.00 AM to 11.30 AM for Sl.No.1 to 9, and 10.00 AM to 11.00 AM for Sl.No.10 to 12).

faq.question: Q9. What is the selection process for DCPU Jangaon posts?
faq.answer: The selection process comprises a written examination with negative marking, an oral test carrying 25 marks, verification of original certificates, and police antecedent verification.

faq.question: Q10. Is this a permanent government job?
faq.answer: No, the engagement is strictly on a contract basis with the District Child Protection Society for one year at a time and confers no right to regularisation.
